properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09: \"how can we link reflow2 and flo2 — flo2 is dependent upon reflow2; we've discussed publisher → subscriber type relationships.\"

WHAT SEARCHING FIRST CHANGED, and it changed the question rather than answering it: most of the linking machinery is DESIGNED AND BUILT, and it has already been RUN on exactly this pair. dec:linked-repos-poc (executed 2026-08-06) composed reflow2, flo2 and dynograph-foundation in a throwaway in-memory graph and found ONE true positive unprompted — ifc:core-api (ours, `library`) against flo2's ifc:model-provider-api (`REST`), 80/100 name match, \"very likely the same contract, but they cannot be connected as either is currently built.\" Nobody told it the answer. So the publisher/subscriber SHAPE is not the open question; dec:pairing-role-placement settled where the role lives, cap:publish-surface and cap:mirror-surface are built, and dec:nested-graphs settled that separately-owned designs are separate graphs.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN IS THE TENSE. Every link so far has been a THING SOMEBODY RAN — a manual composition into a temporary graph, discarded afterwards. A subscription is a standing relationship: flo2 would be continuously answerable to what reflow2 currently publishes, and would learn when it moved. Nothing in the design says how that happens, and the two projects are on different machines, different release cadences and different owners.

THE OPTIONS, in Anthony's framing and with what is cheap or expensive about each recorded beside it rather than argued down:

(A) PULL AT THE EXPORT. flo2 vendors reflow2's committed export (or its published surface via export_surface) and re-composes on each reflow2 release. Cheapest by far, needs nothing new, and rides git which both already use. COUNTER: it is a snapshot, so flo2 learns about a moved contract whenever it next remembers to pull — which is the failure mode this whole question is about, one level up.

(B) PULL AT THE RUNNING SERVER. Once one process holds many designs (cap:graph-registry, reflow2_updates #1), flo2 could hold both graph_ids and ask across them live. COUNTER: gated on the largest outstanding piece of work, and dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs is still proposed. Also flo2's graph_id is `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2` — an opaque mint beside two readable labels — so the addressing story needs a human-facing name first.

(C) A DECLARED DEPENDENCY EDGE BETWEEN DESIGNS, not just between nodes. reflow2 already has req:design-dependencies-declared (accepted, verified) for library versions; the analogue for designs would let a consumer say \"I depend on reflow2's published surface at version X\" and make a stale subscription COMPUTABLE rather than remembered. COUNTER: it is new vocabulary, and dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs and dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency are both still open about what may legitimately cross a design boundary at all.

(D) THE SEAM AS A GATE. flo2's CI composes against reflow2's published export and fails when a contract it consumes has moved — the ci-gate pattern pointed across a boundary instead of inward. COUNTER: it makes reflow2's release able to break flo2's build, which is a real coupling decision and Anthony's to make, not a technical detail.

⚠️ THE BLOCKER IS THE SAME FOR ALL FOUR, AND IT IS ONE MISSING LABEL. dec:linked-repos-poc found it and deliberately did not fix it: REFLOW2 DECLARES NO `required` INTERFACE ANYWHERE. Pairing matches complements, so with nothing required, nothing can ever pair — paired=0 on BOTH pairs, 15 of dynograph-foundation's interfaces and 5 of flo2's landing in dead surface. Its most dangerous number was `unmet_needs: 0`, which reads as \"nothing is missing\" and means \"we never said we needed anything\". Until reflow2 says what it requires, every option above links two designs that cannot be compared. That PoC called declaring them \"the cheapest next step\" — a handful of nodes — and left it to Anthony's word because it is design about reflow2's own boundaries.

AND A SECOND THING NO OPTION ADDRESSES, from reflow2_updates.md #7 (NOT DESIGNED): there are TWO version axes at this seam and only one negotiates. The MCP protocol version negotiates per connection; reflow2's 149-tool surface does not. The toolsnaps stop a surface change landing silently IN THIS REPO and tell flo2 nothing. Whatever subscription shape is chosen has to carry that, or \"clean module\" quietly becomes \"vendored fork\" — which dec:open-reflow2-as-core-module already names as the crux, with the cost falling on @ajs.

NOTHING HERE IS PROMOTED. The options are recorded as considered; the one decision genuinely waiting is whether to declare reflow2's `required` interfaces, which is small, unblocks all four, and is not an agent's to make.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ANSWERED IN PART 2026-08-12 BY A BACKTEST — THE SUBSTRATE IS NOT THE DESIGN EXPORT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This node said the SHAPE was settled and only the TENSE was open. A backtest shows a third thing was open and unnoticed: WHAT THE SUBSCRIPTION WATCHES.

THE METHOD, and it is reusable: rather than build a mechanism and hope, replay real history against failures with KNOWN answers. `reflow2_updates.md` — flo2's hand-written tracker, the manual version of this subscription — went stale in two specific, dated ways. Each was given a window and three candidate signals were scored against it. Read-only; nothing was built.

  §4 CONTRIBUTOR-SCOPED loop_status. The doc was CORRECT when written (2026-08-09 10:21, against v0.26.1 — `loop_status_for` genuinely absent). It landed 3h later in PR #126 and shipped in v0.27.0. The doc became WRONG at its 2026-08-11 re-check. Window: v0.26.1 → v0.27.0.
  §7 THE SEAM CHANGES. `HealIssue.suggested_fix_type` went `&'static str` → `Option`, and five capture tools began REFUSING near-duplicates. Both v0.28.0-only. Window: v0.27.0 → v0.28.0.

RESULTS:

  signal                | §4 input contract | §7 capture refusals | §7 result shape
  design export diff    | 1 hit in 70       | 12 hits in 103      | NO — only "art:heal changed"
  toolsnap diff         | DECISIVE          | DECISIVE            | STRUCTURALLY BLIND

⭐ THE TOOLSNAP DIFF WINS OUTRIGHT ON INPUT CONTRACTS. For §4 it is mechanical and needs no interpretation: `inputSchema.properties` went `{}` → `{contributor_id: …}`. For the capture refusals, `distinct_from` appears with a description that explains the new refusal.

🛑 NOTHING SEES OUTPUT SHAPE. Toolsnaps record `annotations, description, inputSchema, name` — THERE IS NO OUTPUT SCHEMA. So a result-shape change is invisible to every signal reflow2 has, and it is exactly the half most likely to break a generated client.

🛑🛑 AND THE DESIGN EXPORT ACTIVELY LIES. `cap:owed-to-a-contributor` reads `in_progress` at v0.26.1, v0.27.0 AND v0.28.0 — three releases after the capability shipped — because status moves only on the owner's word and nobody went back. A subscription built on design-export status would have told flo2 "still in progress" about working code. THAT IS WORSE THAN SILENCE, and it fully explains how the hand-written doc went wrong: it was not carelessness, the design export AGREED WITH IT.

⇒ **DIFFERENT CONSUMERS NEED DIFFERENT SUBSTRATES.** flo2 calls reflow2's TOOLS; its contract is the tool surface. A sibling consuming reflow2's INTENT would want the design export. Treating "link two designs" as one thing conflates them, and option (A) above (pull at the export) would have watched the wrong artefact.

⚠️ AND THE WINNING SIGNAL IS NOT OBTAINABLE ACROSS THE SEAM. The toolsnaps ship in NEITHER `release.yml` NOR the kit. flo2 has already registered them as `art:reflow2-toolsnaps` with location "github.com/sligara7/reflow2 — tools/toolsnaps/*.json", i.e. GO READ THEM OUT OF OUR REPO. The strongest available signal requires a checkout of the upstream, which defeats consuming a released artifact. TWO CHEAP FOLLOW-ONS THE BACKTEST EARNED: publish the toolsnaps as a release asset, and record OUTPUT schemas in them.

═══ THE PAIRING TRIAL, same day — first time it computed on this pair ═══

`pair_designs` reflow2 → flo2: **paired 0, conflicts 10, unmet_needs 5, dead_surface 2, candidates 1, unclassified 2 ours / 1 theirs.** The blocker this node's PoC recorded (reflow2 declared no `required` interface) cleared in PR #130; reflow2 now declares 9.

  (a) ZERO PAIRS, NOT FOR A FIXABLE REASON. flo2 models `cmp:reflow2-service` as a component it CONTAINS. Pairing matches complements ACROSS a boundary; flo2 drew reflow2 INSIDE its boundary, so there is none. A legitimate model that makes the seam permanently uncomputable by pairing.
  (b) TEN CONFLICTS, NEARLY ALL SPURIOUS. reflow2's dynograph LIBRARY requirements name-matched flo2's REST endpoints at 62–83/100. The one true correspondence scored 61 and landed in `candidates`. Fuzzy names PROPOSE; only a person DISPOSES.
  (c) TWO DESIGNS CAN AGREE BY BEING IDENTICALLY WRONG. Both label the shared boundary `medium: REST`; both MEAN MCP and both say so in `spec` prose. Had roles been complementary they would have PAIRED on a shared falsehood. The tool defends against `unspecified` reading as agreement and has NO defence against two sides stating the same wrong value. A seam check verifies LABEL EQUALITY, never interoperability.

═══ THE GAPS IN LINKING, generalised so they apply to any two reflow2 projects ═══

 1. THE LINK IS NOT A THING. Nothing in either graph records the other exists. A link happens when a human hands two files to a tool: no identity, no owner, no pinned version, no lifecycle. `req:design-dependencies-declared` covers LIBRARY versions and has no analogue for DESIGNS.
 2. CORRESPONDENCE IS INFERRED, NEVER ASSERTED. No shared identifier space, so matching falls back on fuzzy names and re-guesses every run. A human should be able to say "my X IS your Y" and have it stick.
 3. AGREEMENT IS NOT INTEROPERABILITY (see (c) above).
 4. THE LINK IS A RUN, NOT A RELATIONSHIP — the tense problem this node opened with.
 5. THE COMPARISON HIDES ITS OWN SKEW. A 0.27.0 flo2 export was compared against a 0.28.0 reflow2 and nothing said so. ⭐ `dec:fix-the-comparison-before-pointing-it-earlier` step 2 ALREADY DECIDED "a comparison discloses its own confound" for the single-project case and has never been pointed at the cross-project one, which has the same confound and a worse one — the two sides are on different release cadences by construction.
 6. ONLY INTERFACES CROSS. A decision in A that invalidates a capability in B, a shared constraint, readiness gating — the vocabulary for crossing is one node type wide.
 7. READING IS SAFE; WRITING IS NOT. A comparison touches neither store. A propagated gap writes into a graph its owner never agreed to. The git-diff transport survives BECAUSE it never opens the store — a safety property, not an implementation detail.
 8. THE PRECONDITION IS BILATERAL AND NOBODY BUDGETS FOR IT. A seam is only as good as the least-labelled side, `internal` is the DEFAULT so an unlabelled project reports a confidently empty seam, and neither party gets value until both have paid. This is why the whole linking layer has zero instances.
 9. N > 2 IS QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT AND ALREADY MEASURED. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface`: reflow2 and dev_storyflow both depend on dynograph, one as a Rust library and one as REST. A naive pairwise check between the siblings reports ALL-CLEAR — confidently and wrongly — because the conflict lives BELOW both published surfaces. Shared-dependency conflict is a property of the graph, not of any pair in it. Linking N designs is not N-choose-2 links.
properties.name: OPEN — what makes the reflow2→flo2 link a STANDING subscription rather than a run somebody remembers to do?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options in the prose, nothing promoted to intent without Anthony's word. Kept SEPARATE from dec:linked-repos-poc because that node records a RUN and what it proved; this one asks what the relationship should be going forward, which the PoC explicitly did not answer. Kept separate from dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs and dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency because those ask WHAT may cross a design boundary, while this asks WHEN and BY WHAT MECHANISM — one node holding both could only ever be half-answered.

PARTLY ANSWERED 2026-08-12 by a backtest against two dated failures with known answers: the substrate for a TOOL consumer is the toolsnaps, not the design export, whose status field lagged three releases behind a shipped capability. The method — replay real history against failures whose answer is already known — is more reusable than the finding.
